statement: The function returns a result r such that: (1) for every i with 0 <= i < len(r), len(r[i]) = len(nums) and for every integer v, the number of indices k with 0 <= k < len(r[i]) and r[i][k] = v equals the number of indices k with 0 <= k < len(nums) and nums[k] = v; (2) for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < len(r), the lists r[i] and r[j] are not equal; (3) for every list p of 64-bit integers, if len(p) = len(nums) and for every integer v, the number of indices k with 0 <= k < len(p) and p[k] = v equals the number of indices k with 0 <= k < len(nums) and nums[k] = v, then there exists i with 0 <= i < len(r) and r[i] = p.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 8 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10 <= nums[i] <= 10.

statement: Whenever the preconditions hold, the function returns a result r; it does not fail, overflow, panic, or access memory out of bounds.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 8 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10 <= nums[i] <= 10.

statement: Let n = len(nums). Let D be the set of distinct values occurring in nums, i.e., D = { v | there exists i with 0 <= i < n and nums[i] = v }. Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = n! / (product over v in D of count(v, nums)!), where count(v, nums) is the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n and nums[i] = v.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 8 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10 <= nums[i] <= 10.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(r), len(r[i]) = len(nums).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 8 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10 <= nums[i] <= 10.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(r) and every integer v, the number of indices k with 0 <= k < len(r[i]) and r[i][k] = v equals the number of indices k with 0 <= k < len(nums) and nums[k] = v.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 8 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10 <= nums[i] <= 10.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < len(r), the lists r[i] and r[j] are not equal elementwise.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 8 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10 <= nums[i] <= 10.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every list p of 64-bit integers such that len(p) = len(nums) and for every integer v, the number of indices k with 0 <= k < len(p) and p[k] = v equals the number of indices k with 0 <= k < len(nums) and nums[k] = v, there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(r) and r[i] = p.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 8 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10 <= nums[i] <= 10.

statement: If for every i, j with 0 <= i < len(nums) and 0 <= j < len(nums), nums[i] = nums[j], then whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = 1 and r[0] is a list of length len(nums) whose every element equals nums[0].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 8 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10 <= nums[i] <= 10.

statement: Whenever permute_unique(a) returns ra and permute_unique(b) returns rb, for every list p of 64-bit integers, p occurs in ra (i.e., there exists i with 0 <= i < len(ra) and ra[i] = p) if and only if p occurs in rb (i.e., there exists j with 0 <= j < len(rb) and rb[j] = p).
preconditions: For two slices a and b of 64-bit integers: 1 <= len(a) <= 8, 1 <= len(b) <= 8, for every i with 0 <= i < len(a), -10 <= a[i] <= 10, for every i with 0 <= i < len(b), -10 <= b[i] <= 10, len(a) = len(b), and for every integer v, the number of indices k with 0 <= k < len(a) and a[k] = v equals the number of indices k with 0 <= k < len(b) and b[k] = v.

statement: If there exist i, j with 0 <= i < j < len(nums) and nums[i] = nums[j], then whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) < (len(nums))!.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 8 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10 <= nums[i] <= 10.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer v, the total number of pairs (i, k) with 0 <= i < len(r), 0 <= k < len(r[i]), and r[i][k] = v equals len(r) multiplied by the number of indices k with 0 <= k < len(nums) and nums[k] = v.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 8 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10 <= nums[i] <= 10.
